newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-INTERNATIONAL QUARTET IN THE FIRING LINE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-INTERNATIONAL QUARTET IN THE FIRING LINE.

text.p: Four of international rugby's best-known personalities will be in the firing line for their clubs in this weekend's European Cup quarter-finals in France, England and Wales.

Cardiff's Jonathan Davies, former England captain Will Carling, French centre Thomas Castaignede and former Wallaby coach Bob Dwyer are at different stages of their careers but all now face their biggest test of the season so far.
Davies, 34, needs a good match for Cardiff against Bath to press his claims for a recall to the Welsh side to face Australia next month, having been drafted back into the national squad this week.
"The European Cup is probably the main reason why I am enjoying my rugby so much," said Davies..

"Players generally, and I'm no exception, have really taken to it because some of the club rugby you see in Wales can be pretty soft and meaningless. European competition is a totally different standard.
"Being in the Wales squad again is a bonus for me, but all my thoughts at the moment are about beating Bath.
"It is going to be like an international on Saturday. I don't care if it is 3-0, as long as we win."

Carling is back at centre for multi-national Harlequins at Leicester, injuries having curtailed plans to play him at fly-half where he has been trying to carve out a new career since stepping down from the England captaincy.

Now, though, he knows he has no margin for error following Phil De Glanville's appointment as his successor and will be a key man against a Leicester side coached by Dwyer, determined to make a success of his new career in England.
The pair's last meeting in a quarter-final was in the World Cup in Cape Town last year when Rob Andrew settled the issue, but this time Dwyer's men should hold the forward edge.
Leicester can call on Neil Back, playing only his second match since being suspended for jostling the referee in last season's English cup final, and Dwyer is expecting him to impress.
"We had no hesitation about choosing Neil. He has such a wide range of skills and is our fittest player, despite his lack of hard matches."
The winners of the English clash will meet the victors of the all-French game between Dax and Cup holders Toulouse.
On display will be 21-year-old French first-choice centre Castaignede who opposes his international partner, Dax's Richard Dourthe.

Castaignede, whose drop-kick won the Five Nations match against England last season, is regretting his criticism of the English teams in the Cup since his club's 77-point battering by Wasps. "That taught us to keep our feet on the ground," he said.
Brive should ensure a second French name in the semifinals at the expense of Llanelli in the last quarter-final.
